newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita says profits surge, but still cautious.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita says profits surge, but still cautious.

text.p: Japanese electronics giant Matsushita reported a hefty gain in its first-half profits on Friday, but said economic uncertainties cast a shadow on its outlook for the rest of the year.
The firm, Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, said its current profit on a parent company basis surged 29 percent to 53.01 billion yen ($469 million) in the six months to September 30.
"Sales and profit both exceeded our original plans, helped by strong sales in such products as cellular phones and audio visual equipment," Matsushita director Susumu Ishihara told a news conference.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities such as investment in stocks.

Matsushita, whose products are sold under the "National", "Panasonic" and "Technics" brand names, said sales in the information and industrial equipment division grew a robust 12 percent, to 724.8 billion yen ($6.41 billion), helped by a cellular phone boom in Japan.

Ishihara said the company had suffered from a continued decline in prices of its products, particularly audio visual equipment, but higher sales volume as well as the weaker yen more than offset this.
Only its electronic components business, which includes computer chips, saw a sales decline -- of five percent.
Despite the strong first-half performance, which also exceeded market expectations, Matsushita said continuing price declines could depress its second-half earnings.

The firm had been widely expected to revise upward its full-year profit forecast. Instead, it stuck to its May projection for a parent current profit of 130 billion yen ($1.15 billion) in the year to March 1997.
Ishihara said that a fall in its product prices in Japan and overseas markets cut profits by as much as 38.4 billion yen ($339 million) in the first half.
"It is hard to predict the course of the economy after the turn of the year, while the yen's rate remains unpredictable," he said.
The yen is currently trading at around 113 to the dollar. This compares with the all-time high of 79.75 to the dollar it touched in April last year.
